_meta.description: Scripted tactical positions for the eval harness. Each position is a board given as stone lists (coordinates are [x, y], 0-based, x = column left-to-right, y = row top-to-bottom), the side to move, and an expectation. Expectation types: 'win' (any move that wins immediately passes) or 'moves' (the chosen move must be one of the listed squares). Positions were verified programmatically (see tests/test_evaluate.py::test_tactical_positions_are_sound): no side has already won, every expected move is legal, and for 'moves' positions the listed squares are exactly the moves that satisfy the tactical requirement (verified exhaustively, including a VCF search for the forced-win positions).

positions.description: Black has four in a row with both ends open; either end wins.
positions.name: Take the win — horizontal open four

positions.description: Black has four in a column with both ends open; either end wins.
positions.name: Take the win — vertical open four

positions.description: Black has four on the main diagonal with both ends open.
positions.name: Take the win — diagonal open four

positions.description: Black has four on the anti-diagonal with both ends open.
positions.name: Take the win — anti-diagonal open four

positions.description: Black's four is blocked at one end by White; only the open end wins.
positions.name: Take the win — half-open four

positions.description: Black's four has a hole in the middle; only the gap square completes five.
positions.name: Take the win — fill the gap

positions.description: Black's diagonal four has a hole in the middle; only the gap square wins.
positions.name: Take the win — fill the diagonal gap

positions.description: Black's four runs along the left edge; both ends win (one is the corner).
positions.name: Take the win — at the board edge

positions.description: Black has two fours crossing at (7,7); three squares win, one of them completes both.
positions.name: Take the win — two fours at once

positions.description: White threatens five on the row; Black's stone blocks one end, so there is exactly one square to play. (A true open four — both ends open — cannot be blocked with one move; these block positions are half-open fours.)
positions.name: Block — horizontal four

positions.description: White threatens five in a column; exactly one square blocks it.
positions.name: Block — vertical four

positions.description: White threatens five on the diagonal; exactly one square blocks it.
positions.name: Block — diagonal four

positions.description: White's four starts at the left edge, so the edge itself blocks one end; exactly one square blocks it.
positions.name: Block — four at the board edge

positions.description: White's four has a hole in the middle; only the gap square stops the five.
positions.name: Block — four with a gap

positions.description: White has an open four (unblockable — both ends win), but Black has an open four too. Blocking White loses; Black must take the win first.
positions.name: Counter-win — opponent has an open four

positions.description: Black has a tempting open three (extending it makes a four), but White threatens five next move. Extending the three loses on the spot; Black must block.
positions.name: Avoid the trap — block instead of attacking

positions.description: Black has a horizontal three and a vertical three meeting at the corner (7,7). Only (7,7) completes both fours at once — two independent threats White cannot block with one move. Every other move creates at most one threat.
positions.name: Create a double threat — the corner move

positions.description: White has a horizontal three and a vertical three meeting at (7,7), both with open ends. If Black plays anywhere else, White plays (7,7) and creates two open fours at once (four winning squares) — blocking just one end of one four does not help. (7,7) is the only move that stops both threats.
positions.name: Find the only defence — the corner move

positions.description: Black has a horizontal three (6,6)-(8,6) and a vertical two (8,4)-(8,5) sharing the stone at (8,6). (9,6), (10,6) and (8,3) all start forced sequences of fours: each four forces White's only block, and the sequence ends in five at (8,7). (8,7) and (8,2) look forcing but are traps: after White's block the attack dies. Passes iff the chosen move starts a forced win (VCF search).
positions.name: Forced win — VCF sequence (horizontal + vertical)

positions.description: Black has a diagonal three (6,6)-(8,8) and a vertical two (8,6)-(8,7) sharing the stone at (8,8). (9,9), (10,10) and (8,5) all start forced sequences of fours ending in five at (8,9). (8,9) and (8,4) look forcing but are traps: after White's block the attack dies. Passes iff the chosen move starts a forced win (VCF search).
positions.name: Forced win — VCF sequence (diagonal + vertical)
